name: Athlai
overview: Athlai was a male figure noted in the book of Ezra as a descendant of Bebai. He is uniquely identified by his association with a foreign wife, which was significant in the post-exilic community's efforts to maintain covenantal purity. No additional tribal affiliation or personal notes are recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Athlai is a proper name possibly meaning 'YHWH is exalted' or 'oldest of YHWH.' This reflects a theocentric meaning, emphasizing the exaltation of the Lord, though the name was not given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Athlai as a descendant of Bebai. Beyond this lineage, no other family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Athlai's significance in Scripture arises from his inclusion among those who had married foreign wives, a matter addressed in Ezra 10:28. This highlights the post-exilic community's commitment to covenant faithfulness and the challenges faced in restoring Israel's purity in accordance with God's commands. His mention underscores the broader narrative of repentance and reform under Ezra's leadership.
